headline: Council delays $2,689,790 first-year trash contract to November 9 and passes a one-year data center moratorium.
summary: The council voted 4-3 to ask federal officials to reopen the investigation into former Methuen Police Department leadership. It also approved a home rule petition for paving some unaccepted roads, 8-1, and a resolution seeking funds for the Arlington neighborhood infrastructure project. A resolution on health insurance eligibility for elected officials failed.
decisions: Approved appointment of Jeffrey Farrely as superintendent of building maintenance, unanimously.
Approved appointment of Michael Welch to the Conservation Commission, unanimously.
Approved resolution asking state and federal officials for funding for the Arlington neighborhood infrastructure project, unanimously.
Approved National Grid grant to install a new pole on Taft Avenue, unanimously.
Approved $32,891.63 contract with United Compressor & Pump Services to replace a sewer pump, unanimously.
Approved $38,684.21 renewal of Cityworks asset management software, unanimously.
Approved $72,800 one-year grant-funded position to digitize local history, unanimously.
Approved $29,000 engineering contract with Andrew Brockway & Associates for the Timony School roof, 8-1.
Approved $138,129 contract with Northeast Behavioral Health for a mental health and jail diversion program, unanimously.
Tabled the Waste Management trash and recycling contract to a November 9 workshop and special meeting.
Approved resolution calling for the federal investigation into former Methuen police leadership to be reopened, 4-3.
Approved acceptance of $27,999.02 bulletproof vest grant, unanimously.
Approved acceptance of $48,759.90 federal municipal road safety grant, unanimously.
Accepted gift of equipment from Planet Fitness for the fire department, unanimously.
Approved one-year moratorium on data centers in Methuen, as amended, unanimously.
Approved acceptance of $36,000 recycling dividends grant, unanimously.
Approved amendment sending $2,000 to American Legion Post 122 for the Veterans Day Parade band.
Approved $33,000 transfer from Edwin J. Castle Fund for awards, with one abstention.
Failed to approve resolution on GIC health insurance eligibility for elected officials, on a unanimous no vote.
Approved home rule petition to allow paving of certain unaccepted roads, 8-1.
Tabled industrial zoning ordinance update to send it to a joint public hearing, unanimously.
discussion: Trash contract timing: Members asked for more time to review the Waste Management contract, and the company said a delay could raise truck rental costs.
Federal investigation letter: Speakers urged the council to sign the letter and asked councilors with past ties to the 2017 contract to step aside.
Housing Authority trash service: Housing Authority staff and condo owners argued over whether the city should keep serving the authority and whether condos should get curbside service.
GIC health insurance eligibility: Members discussed whether elected officials and part-time workers should qualify for city health coverage, and the resolution failed.
Arlington water project: Members said water service lines with unknown materials need replacement, and that remaining phases cost about $88 million.
